public_rationale: GPT-4’s technical report expressly describes next-token prediction as its pretraining objective. That supports the ordinary foundation reading of autocompletion. The qualification matters: the same report describes factuality improvements from post-training, and RARR demonstrates external grounding and revision. A stronger claim that contemporary systems contained no factuality-oriented components would not be supported.
limitations: The outcome depends on reading built on as the foundation rather than every component of a deployed system.
Predicting text does not imply an inability to represent facts.
The conclusion concerns language models, not all generative architectures.

our_interpretation: In context, technology refers to contemporary general-purpose language models.
The plain reading of built on is their foundational training objective: predicting text continuations rather than verifying each assertion against facts.
This does not mean that factuality-oriented fine-tuning, retrieval, or external verification were absent.
With no common reporting cycle, the current-system observation window is calendar 2023 through publication.

criteria.contradiction_condition: Primary documentation establishes factual verification as the foundational mechanism of the contemporary systems instead of predictive text completion.
